gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the LiTime 12V 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth and LiHeat Self-Heating batteries it recommended top out at 4P4S (16 batteries, 51.2 V, 20.48 kWh), ship switched off and need a charger connected to turn on, and carry no CAN/RS485 inverter communication (LiTime reserves that for its ComFlex line), while Redodo's otherwise identical 4P4S Group 24 battery is excluded by the maker from golf-cart, water-pump, electric-jack and mower duty.
standout_why: BatteryTrail (cited) lists series/parallel ceilings for Battle Born (to 48 V), Renogy Pro (parallel only, up to 8), SOK (4S10P) and Dakota (2S4P) but writes 'See manual' for LiTime and does not cover the Group 24 Bluetooth, LiHeat, Redodo or Vatrer models at all; it also says nothing about inverter comms, alternator charging or activation. ExploringOffGrid (cited) gives only generic 4S4P category guidance with no model attached and no exclusions. LiTime's own Victron blog (rank 7, not cited) is the only result touching comms, and it covers 300Ah-class batteries, not the 100Ah picks.
decides: Confirms the LiTime 12V 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth ($311.09) as the value pick for a 12 V bank that may later grow to 24 V or 48 V, since LiTime, Redodo and (per the maker) the LiTime LiHeat all allow 4S4P where Renogy Pro is parallel-only and Dakota stops at 2S. It adds two conditions none of the rival pages give: a buyer must have a LiFePO4 charger on hand to switch a new LiTime Bluetooth battery on, and anyone wanting the battery to talk to a Victron GX / inverter should not buy any of ChatGPT's three picks, because none of them has CAN or RS485. For cold climates the LiTime LiHeat ($368.99) is the only candidate whose maker says it can heat from its own stored energy before charging; Vatrer's heated model heats only while a charger is connected.
